title: Render modes
summary: Where a component runs (server or browser) and whether it is interactive.

predict.title: No render mode
options: Count: 0, and an error appears in the console
predict.explanation: **Count: 0.** Nothing happens. Without `@rendermode`, the page is **static SSR**: the server sends HTML and disposes the component. The `@onclick` handler is never wired up, because no C# is listening in the browser or on the server. There is no error, which is why this bug is easy to miss.

predict.title: Interactive Server
options: Count: 3. Each click goes to the server over a WebSocket, and the server sends back only what changed.
Count: 3. Each click reloads the whole page with a normal HTTP request.
Count: 3. The C# runs in the browser, so nothing goes over the network.
Count: 0, because you must call `StateHasChanged()` after `count++`.
predict.explanation: **Count: 3.** Each click is sent to the server over the SignalR **WebSocket**. The server runs `count++`, re-renders, and sends back only the **diff** (the changed text). You don't need `StateHasChanged()`: Blazor re-renders automatically after an event handler.

predict.title: How many times?
options: Once in the server console and once in the browser console
Never, because `Console.WriteLine` doesn't work in Blazor
predict.explanation: **Twice, both in the server console** (the terminal where `dotnet run` runs). The first time is during **prerendering** (static HTML). The second is when the circuit starts and the component becomes interactive. With `prerender: false`, it prints only once.

predict.title: WebAssembly console
predict.body:
Same as C, but the component is in the `.Client` project and uses:

```razor
@rendermode InteractiveWebAssembly
```

**After one full page load, where does "C initialized" appear?**
options: Only in the server console, once
Only in the browser console, once
Once in the server console and once in the browser console
predict.explanation: **Once in the server console** (prerendering happens on the server) and **once in the browser's dev tools console** (the WebAssembly render runs in the browser, so `Console.WriteLine` goes there).

practice.title: A static page
practice.task:
Write the `/static` page: a counter button, plus a line that shows `RendererInfo.Name` and `RendererInfo.IsInteractive`. Use **no** render mode.

In a real app this page renders once and the button does nothing. Keep that in mind for the quiz.
practice.hint: `RendererInfo` is available in every component; you don't need to inject anything.

checks.label: No `@rendermode` (this page must stay static)
checks.hint: Delete the `@rendermode` line: static is the default.

checks.label: A button with `@onclick` that changes the count

practice.title: Make it interactive on the server
practice.task: This counter does nothing when you click it. Make it run as **Interactive Server**, so the clicks work. Don't add anything that isn't needed.

checks.label: A button with `@onclick` that changes the count
No `StateHasChanged()` call (Blazor re-renders after an event handler on its own)
checks.hint: Remove `StateHasChanged()`: it is not needed after `@onclick`.

practice.title: Run it in the browser
practice.task:
Write a `/wasm` page with the same counter and `RendererInfo` line, but running in **WebAssembly** (the C# runs in the browser).

In a Blazor Web App this file goes in the `.Client` project.

checks.label: A button with `@onclick` that changes the count
No `StateHasChanged()` call (Blazor re-renders after an event handler on its own)
checks.hint: Remove `StateHasChanged()`: it is not needed after `@onclick`.

practice.title: Stop the double run
practice.task: This page prints "Loaded" **twice** in the server console on every full page load. Change only the render mode so it prints **once**, and keep it Interactive Server.
practice.hint: It runs twice because of **prerendering**. A render mode can be created with `new` and options.

checks.label: Prerendering is off: `@rendermode @(new InteractiveServerRenderMode(prerender: false))`
checks.hint: Write the mode as an expression: `@rendermode @(new ...(prerender: false))`.

checks.label: `OnInitialized` still writes the line
checks.hint: Keep the `OnInitialized` method as it was.

practice.title: The /modes page (from scratch)
practice.task:
Close the theory and build a `/modes` page with **Interactive Server** that shows:

- the render mode name and whether it is interactive
- a click counter
- the time of the last click

checks.label: A button with `@onclick` that changes the count
A `DateTime` field stores the last click
checks.hint: Declare a field such as `private DateTime? lastClick;`.

checks.label: The click handler sets it to the current time
The page displays that field
checks.hint: Show the field in the markup, for example `@lastClick`.

checks.label: No `StateHasChanged()` call (Blazor re-renders after an event handler on its own)
checks.hint: Remove `StateHasChanged()`: it is not needed after `@onclick`.

quiz.body: You open `/server` (Interactive Server) with the browser dev tools on the **Network** tab, filtered to **WS**. What do you see?
options: Nothing: Blazor Server uses plain HTTP requests
A new WebSocket for every click
One WebSocket (`_blazor`) that stays open while you are on the page
quiz.explanation: Interactive Server keeps **one SignalR connection** (a WebSocket to `_blazor`) open. Clicks and UI diffs travel over it.

quiz.body: On the first visit to `/wasm` (Interactive WebAssembly), what does the browser download before the page becomes interactive?
options: The .NET runtime and the app's assemblies (`_framework/*.wasm` and `.dll` files)
A SignalR client, then nothing else
The C# source files, compiled in the browser
quiz.explanation: WebAssembly mode runs real .NET in the browser, so it first downloads the **runtime and the assemblies** from `_framework/`.

quiz.body: On `/static` (no render mode) you use **View Source**. What do you find?
options: An empty `<div>` filled in later by JavaScript
Only a `<script>` tag that loads Blazor
The full HTML of the page, including `Count: 0`
quiz.explanation: Static SSR sends **complete HTML** from the server. That is all the page is: nothing is listening for clicks.

quiz.body: Why does the button on `/static` do nothing, with no error?
options: After rendering, the component is disposed and no circuit or WebAssembly runtime is listening for events
quiz.explanation: With static SSR, the component is rendered once to HTML and disposed. No circuit or WebAssembly runtime is listening, so `@onclick` is never wired up. It fails silently.

quiz.body: What does `RendererInfo.Name` show on the `/static` page?
quiz.explanation: `Static` for static SSR, `Server` for Interactive Server, `WebAssembly` for WebAssembly. `IsInteractive` is `false` on a static page.

quiz.body: During **prerendering** of an Interactive Server page, what is `RendererInfo.IsInteractive`?
options: `false`, because the prerender is static HTML; it becomes `true` once the circuit starts
quiz.explanation: The prerender is a **static** render on the server, so `IsInteractive` is `false` (and `Name` is `Static`). After the circuit starts, the component renders again as `Server` / `true`. This is why you may briefly see a disabled-looking UI.

quiz.body: In a Blazor Web App, where must a component with `@rendermode InteractiveWebAssembly` or `InteractiveAuto` live?
options: In the `.Client` project, so it is part of the code sent to the browser
In the server project, next to `App.razor`
Anywhere: the mode decides where it runs
quiz.explanation: Code that may run in the browser must be in the **`.Client`** project. Otherwise the browser never gets the assembly, and the route returns 404.

quiz.body: What does **Interactive Auto** do on a user's first visit?
options: It uses Interactive Server while the WebAssembly files download in the background; later visits use WebAssembly
It picks the faster mode at random
quiz.explanation: It starts with Interactive Server for a fast first render while downloading the WebAssembly bundle in the background. Later visits use WebAssembly. The component must live in the `.Client` project and work in both places.

quiz.body: After `@onclick` runs `count++` in an interactive component, do you need `StateHasChanged()`?
options: No: Blazor re-renders the component after an event handler on its own
quiz.explanation: Blazor calls `StateHasChanged` for you **after an event handler**. You need it yourself only when state changes outside an event, for example in a timer callback.

quiz.body: You open an AI-generated Blazor Web App and no page has `@rendermode`, yet every button works. Where is the render mode most likely set?
quiz.explanation: A render mode on `<Routes>` in `App.razor` applies to **every page**. Static SSR is the default, so if buttons work, the mode is set somewhere.

interview.question: What are the Blazor render modes?
interview.modelAnswer: Static SSR (the default: HTML only, not interactive), Interactive Server (runs on the server over a SignalR circuit), Interactive WebAssembly (runs in the browser), and Interactive Auto (Server first, then WebAssembly once it is downloaded).

interview.question: When would you choose Server over WebAssembly?
interview.modelAnswer: When you want a fast first load, direct access to server resources (database, secrets), or small client devices, and users have a stable, low-latency connection. Typical for internal business apps.

interview.question: When would you choose WebAssembly over Server?
interview.modelAnswer: When you want no round trip per UI event, offline support, less server memory and connection load, or hosting as static files (a CDN). The trade-off is a larger first download, and that all client code is public.

interview.question: What does Auto mode do?
interview.modelAnswer: It starts with Interactive Server for a fast first render while downloading the WebAssembly bundle in the background. Later visits use WebAssembly. The component must live in the `.Client` project and work in both places.

interview.question: What is prerendering and what problem can it cause?
interview.modelAnswer: The server renders interactive components to HTML first, for a fast first paint and SEO, then renders them again when they become interactive. Lifecycle methods run twice, so data can load twice or flicker. Fix it with `prerender: false` or by persisting state with `[PersistentState]` (.NET 10).

interview.question: How does the UI update in Interactive Server?
interview.modelAnswer: The browser sends the event over a SignalR WebSocket. The server runs the handler, re-renders the component, compares it with the previous render tree, and sends only the diff. The browser then patches the DOM.

interview.question: Why does a button do nothing on a static page?
interview.modelAnswer: With static SSR, the component is rendered once to HTML and disposed. No circuit or WebAssembly runtime is listening, so `@onclick` is never wired up. It fails silently.

interview.question: How do you tell which mode a component is running in?
interview.modelAnswer: Look for `@rendermode` on the component, on its usage, or globally on `<Routes>` in `App.razor`. At runtime, check `RendererInfo.Name` / `RendererInfo.IsInteractive` (and `AssignedRenderMode`).
